reason: The text explicitly names multiple characters who are not leaders in the political or administrative sense. Most significantly, Micaiah (מִיכָיְהוּ) and Zidkijah son of Kenaanah (צִדְקִיָּה בֶן־ כְּנַעֲנָה) are named prophets, not political or military leaders. While the text does feature three kings (Jehoshaphat of Judah, Ahab of Israel, and the King of Aram) and Amon the city officer—all legitimate leaders—the inclusion of the named prophets invalidates the claim that only leaders are named characters. Prophets are religious figures whose authority derives from God's word rather than from political office.
